why: The state is (column used so far, prefix of target built). Only the count of each letter per column matters, so dp[j] += dp[j-1] * count[col][target[j-1]] while you sweep columns left to right. It is a 2-D DP compressed into one array, which is how it fits the week's 1-D DP theme, updated backwards like 0/1 knapsack so each column is used once.
hints: Strictly increasing indices means each column contributes at most one character, in order.
Precompute cnt[col][c], the number of words with letter c at column col. Picking column col for target[j] multiplies the ways by that count.
dp[0] = 1. For each column, for j from m down to 1, set dp[j] += dp[j-1] * cnt[col][target[j-1]] mod 1e9+7. Answer dp[m]. O(width * (n + m)).
pitfalls: Iterate j downward inside a column. Going upward would reuse the same column for two target letters.
Take the modulo at every multiply.
Different words at the same column are different ways, so multiply by the count rather than adding 1.
